rows: Sliding hip screw or cephalomedullary nail

hypercalcemia.name: Hypercalcemia
hypercalcemia.scope: Primary hyperparathyroidism, malignancy-associated hypercalcemia, milk-alkali syndrome, IV saline resuscitation, calcitonin, bisphosphonates
hypercalcemia.core: Elevated calcium causes stones, constipation, polyuria, weakness, and neuropsychiatric changes; PTH distinguishes hormone-driven disease from other causes.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Parathyroid adenoma/hyperplasia, malignancy, prolonged immobilization
Thiazides, lithium, excess vitamin D or calcium/absorbable alkali, granulomatous disease

rows.label: Clues
items: Dehydration, nausea, abdominal pain, reduced reflexes; ECG may show shortened QT
★ **Calcium >14 mg/dL**, confusion, arrhythmia, or severe volume depletion → urgent treatment
Primary hyperparathyroidism often asymptomatic; malignancy-associated disease tends to progress rapidly

rows.label: Pathophys
items: PTH promotes bone resorption and renal calcium retention while increasing phosphate excretion
Hypercalcemia impairs renal concentration → dehydration, reduced calcium clearance, self-reinforcing elevation

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ Confirm with repeat total/albumin-adjusted or **ionized calcium**, especially with altered proteins or critical illness
★ **Intact PTH first**; elevated or inappropriately normal → PTH-dependent
Suppressed PTH → PTHrP, vitamin D metabolites, malignancy/myeloma evaluation guided by context
Primary disease versus FHH → urine calcium; clearance ratio <0.01 favors FHH, with overlap
Parathyroid imaging localizes before surgery; never establishes biochemical diagnosis

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ Severe/symptomatic → **IV isotonic saline**, then calcitonin for rapid temporary lowering
★ **IV zoledronic acid** for sustained malignancy control; denosumab if severe renal limitations/refractory disease
Calcitriol-mediated disease → glucocorticoids; dialysis for refractory life-threatening elevation or inability to hydrate
Primary disease: surgery for symptoms, age <50, calcium >1 above ULN, osteoporosis/fracture, stones, eGFR <60
Stop causative supplements/drugs; loop diuretic only for fluid overload, not routine calcium elimination

rows.label: Complications
items: Nephrolithiasis, nephrocalcinosis, AKI, osteoporosis/fractures, pancreatitis
Calcitonin tachyphylaxis after 48–72 hours; antiresorptives can cause hypocalcemia

rows.label: Prevention
items: Hydration, avoid excess calcium/alkali; monitor calcium, renal function, and bone density when observing primary disease

rows.label: Mimics
items: FHH: lifelong mild elevation, family history, hypocalciuria; surgery ineffective
Pseudohypercalcemia: high protein-bound calcium but normal ionized fraction

hypercalcemia.evidence: Not checked online; established calcium evaluation and emergency management.

inflammatory-bowel-disease.name: Inflammatory bowel disease
inflammatory-bowel-disease.scope: Crohn disease, ulcerative colitis, extraintestinal manifestations (erythema nodosum, pyoderma gangrenosum, uveitis), toxic megacolon, colorectal cancer risk, biologic therapy
inflammatory-bowel-disease.core: Chronic relapsing intestinal inflammation: Crohn disease affects any gastrointestinal segment; ulcerative colitis begins in the rectum.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Family history, young adulthood; smoking worsens Crohn disease
NSAIDs and enteric infections can precipitate flares

rows.label: Clues
items: Chronic diarrhea, abdominal pain, weight loss, anemia; children may have growth failure
Arthritis, uveitis, erythema nodosum, pyoderma gangrenosum; PSC particularly associated with UC
★ Severe colitis: fever, tachycardia, frequent bloody stools; distention suggests **toxic megacolon**

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Dysregulated mucosal immune response to intestinal microbiota in genetically susceptible hosts

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ Stool **C. difficile** testing and cultures before attributing worsening diarrhea to inflammation
Fecal calprotectin supports intestinal inflammation; **ileocolonoscopy with biopsies** confirms
Suspected small-bowel disease or abscess → MR enterography; avoid capsule with suspected stricture
Fulminant colitis → abdominal radiograph and limited sigmoidoscopy; avoid full colonoscopy

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ Acute severe UC → hospitalization, **IV methylprednisolone**, fluids, VTE prophylaxis
Steroid-refractory severe UC → infliximab or cyclosporine; perforation or megacolon → urgent colectomy
★ Steroids induce remission only; **never maintenance**
Crohn abscess → antibiotics and drainage before immunosuppression

rows.label: Complications
items: Fistulas, strictures, obstruction and B12 deficiency in Crohn; colectomy does not cure Crohn
Colonic disease → colorectal cancer; active inflammation → venous thromboembolism

rows.label: Prevention
items: ★ Colonic disease → surveillance colonoscopy beginning about **8 years** after onset; PSC → immediately
Vaccinate and screen TB/HBV before biologics; smoking cessation for Crohn

rows.label: Mimics
items: IBS: no bleeding, weight loss or inflammatory markers
Ischemic colitis: abrupt pain followed by hematochezia, vascular risk

informed-consent-and-capacity.name: Informed consent and capacity
informed-consent-and-capacity.scope: Decision-making capacity, informed consent, emergency exception (implied consent), refusal of treatment, AMA discharge
informed-consent-and-capacity.core: A capable adult may accept or refuse treatment after understanding its benefits, material risks, alternatives, and consequences of refusal.

rows.label: Principle
items: ★ Capacity: **understand, appreciate, reason, communicate choice**; specific to decision, fluctuating
Competence: legal determination; diagnosis, age, or disagreement alone does not establish incapacity

rows.label: Do
items: ★ Explain benefits, material risks, alternatives/no treatment; **qualified interpreter and teach-back**
Correct delirium, intoxication, pain, communication barriers; reassess capacity
AMA request: assess capacity, explore barriers, offer safer plan, document discussion and follow-up

rows.label: Don't
items: Capable refusal → respect choice, including life-saving treatment; avoid coercion or abandonment
No valid consent → possible **battery**; signed form alone insufficient

rows.label: Exceptions
items: ★ Emergency + incapacity + no available surrogate/directive → implied consent for necessary treatment
★ Parents refuse minor's life-saving transfusion → **treat emergency**; seek court authority if feasible
Incapacity without emergency → authorized surrogate; involve patient to remaining ability

rows.label: Traps
items: Psychiatric illness does not automatically remove capacity; assess the specific decision
Suicide danger may justify protective detention despite expressed desire to leave
New material procedure or substantially changed risk → renewed consent discussion

informed-consent-and-capacity.evidence: Not checked online; established consent/capacity ethics; emergency and minor-consent law varies by jurisdiction.

invasive-fungal-infections.name: Invasive fungal infections
invasive-fungal-infections.scope: Invasive aspergillosis, allergic bronchopulmonary aspergillosis (ABPA), mucormycosis, candidemia, amphotericin B, voriconazole, systemic corticosteroids
invasive-fungal-infections.core: Fungal syndromes range from allergic airway disease to lethal tissue invasion; immune status and imaging guide testing and treatment.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Prolonged neutropenia/transplant → molds; DKA, glucocorticoids or iron overload → mucormycosis
Central lines, TPN, abdominal surgery, broad antibiotics → invasive Candida
ABPA: asthma or cystic fibrosis; hypersensitivity rather than tissue invasion

rows.label: Clues
items: Invasive aspergillosis: fever despite antibiotics, pleuritic pain, hemoptysis, pulmonary nodules
★ **Black nasal/palatal eschar**, facial pain, ophthalmoplegia → rhinocerebral mucormycosis
Candidemia: sepsis, persistent positive blood cultures; metastatic eye, heart or deep-organ infection
ABPA: recurrent wheeze, brown mucus plugs, fleeting pulmonary infiltrates

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Angioinvasive molds cause vascular thrombosis, infarction and necrosis
Candida translocates through damaged gut or colonizes intravascular devices, then disseminates hematogenously

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ Suspected mold pneumonia → **chest CT**, bronchoscopy/BAL or tissue biopsy
Aspergillus galactomannan in serum/BAL; β-D-glucan supports several fungi but usually negative in mucormycosis
Necrotic sinus lesion → urgent endoscopic biopsy for histology/culture; do not await blood cultures
Candidemia → repeat blood cultures until clear; assess source and metastatic foci
ABPA: Aspergillus-IgE + total IgE ≥500 IU/mL; two of eosinophilia, Aspergillus-IgG, CT bronchiectasis/infiltrates

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ Aspergillosis → **voriconazole** or isavuconazole; evaluate interactions and liver function
★ Mucormycosis → **liposomal amphotericin B + urgent surgical debridement**; correct DKA/immunosuppression
Candidemia → echinocandin such as micafungin; step down to fluconazole when stable, susceptible and cleared
Remove implicated line when feasible; uncomplicated candidemia → ≥14 days after clearance and symptom resolution
ABPA → prednisolone or itraconazole; recurrent flares → both; avoid steroids for untreated invasive disease

rows.label: Complications
items: CNS dissemination, massive hemoptysis, blindness, endocarditis; high mortality if treatment delayed
Amphotericin → AKI, hypokalemia/hypomagnesemia; voriconazole → visual effects, hepatotoxicity

rows.label: Prevention
items: Selected high-risk prolonged neutropenia → posaconazole prophylaxis; line hygiene and antibiotic stewardship

rows.label: Mimics
items: Pseudomonas ecthyma gangrenosum: necrotic skin lesions with bacterial sepsis
Bacterial abscess: pyogenic cultures; malignancy: tissue without invasive organisms

lung-cancer.name: Lung cancer
lung-cancer.scope: Non-small cell, small cell, paraneoplastic syndromes, Pancoast, screening
lung-cancer.core: Persistent cough, hemoptysis, weight loss, or a suspicious lung lesion requires tissue diagnosis and staging before treatment selection.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Smoking, radon, asbestos, occupational carcinogens, prior thoracic radiation; adenocarcinoma also occurs in never-smokers

rows.label: Clues
items: Recurrent focal pneumonia, hoarseness, clubbing, unexplained pleural effusion
★ **Pancoast tumor**: shoulder/ulnar-arm pain + ipsilateral Horner syndrome
SVC obstruction: facial swelling, neck-vein distention; cord compression or airway compromise requires urgent action

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Bronchogenic malignant transformation → local invasion, lymphatic spread, hematogenous metastasis
Ectopic hormone production and immune cross-reactivity cause paraneoplastic syndromes

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ Suspicious finding → **contrast chest CT**; biopsy easiest site that establishes highest stage
Central lesion/nodes → bronchoscopy/EBUS; peripheral lesion → CT-guided biopsy; effusion → cytology
PET/CT for extracranial staging, brain MRI for selected stages/small-cell disease; pulmonary function before resection
Molecular profiling and PD-L1 guide advanced NSCLC treatment; suspicious nodes often require pathologic staging

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ Early operable NSCLC → **surgical resection + nodal evaluation**; inoperable localized → stereotactic radiation
Locally advanced NSCLC → combined systemic treatment/radiation ± surgery in selected patients
Metastatic NSCLC → biomarker-directed agents or immunotherapy/chemotherapy
★ Small-cell → **platinum + etoposide**, stage-dependent radiation/immunotherapy; surgery rarely used

rows.label: Complications
items: Brain/bone/adrenal/liver metastases, malignant effusion, thrombosis, respiratory failure
Radiation pneumonitis; checkpoint inhibitors → immune pneumonitis/endocrinopathies

rows.label: Prevention
items: ★ USPSTF: **annual low-dose CT**, age 50–80, ≥20 pack-years, current smoking or quit <15 years
Stop after 15 quit-years or limited curative candidacy; **ACS omits quit-time restriction**
Smoking cessation and radon mitigation; chest radiographs do not substitute for screening CT

rows.label: Mimics
items: TB/fungal granuloma: microbiologic evidence; PET uptake not specific for cancer
Hamartoma: fat/popcorn calcification; pneumonia: clinical/radiographic response to antibiotics

lung-cancer.evidence: Screening checked 2026-10-30: [USPSTF 2021](https://www.uspreventiveservicestaskforce.org/uspstf/recommendation/lung-cancer-screening), [ACS 2023 guideline](https://acsjournals.onlinelibrary.wiley.com/doi/10.3322/caac.21811); treatment: established stage-based framework.

mesenteric-ischemia.name: Mesenteric ischemia
mesenteric-ischemia.scope: Acute mesenteric ischemia, chronic mesenteric ischemia, ischemic colitis, CTA abdomen, colonoscopy
mesenteric-ischemia.core: Intestinal hypoperfusion causes severe abdominal pain; early examination and lactate may appear deceptively reassuring.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: AF, recent MI, valvular disease → embolism; diffuse atherosclerosis → arterial thrombosis
Shock, heart failure, vasopressors → nonocclusive ischemia; hypercoagulability → mesenteric venous thrombosis

rows.label: Clues
items: ★ **Pain out of proportion** to abdominal examination; sudden onset especially with embolism
Nausea, diarrhea, later bloody stool; guarding/rebound suggests transmural infarction
Right-sided colonic disease or severe pain without bleeding → investigate proximal mesenteric occlusion

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Oxygen supply failure injures mucosa before serosa; bacterial translocation and necrosis follow
Collateral flow usually protects intestine until acute major occlusion or multivessel chronic disease

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ **CTA abdomen/pelvis with arterial and venous phases** immediately for suspected acute ischemia
Do not delay lifesaving contrast imaging solely because of renal dysfunction
CBC, metabolic panel, lactate/ABG; normal early lactate does not exclude disease
Avoid colonoscopy with peritonitis, perforation, or suspected gangrene; minimal insufflation when safe

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ Acute mesenteric: NPO, **IV saline, piperacillin-tazobactam, unfractionated heparin**; urgent vascular/surgical consult
★ **Peritonitis or infarcted bowel → emergency laparotomy**, resect nonviable bowel and restore flow
Arterial occlusion without peritonitis → urgent endovascular/open revascularization based on anatomy and expertise
Nonocclusive disease → restore perfusion, reduce vasoconstrictors; selected catheter-directed papaverine
Isolated mesenteric venous thrombosis without infarction → anticoagulation

rows.label: Complications
items: Bowel necrosis, perforation, sepsis, multiorgan failure, death
Short-bowel syndrome after extensive resection; reperfusion injury, recurrent thrombosis
Ischemic colitis can heal with segmental stricture

rows.label: Prevention
items: ★ **Anticoagulate AF when eligible**; smoking cessation, statin, atherosclerotic risk reduction
Treat low-flow triggers promptly; thrombophilia evaluation for selected venous thrombosis

rows.label: Mimics
items: Infectious colitis: exposure/fever, stool pathogen identification
Pancreatitis: epigastric/back pain with lipase elevation
Perforated viscus: early rigid abdomen/free air; bowel obstruction: transition point on CT

table.title: Chronic disease versus colonic ischemia
rows: Postprandial pain, food fear, weight loss
Cramps then hematochezia; older low-flow patient
Fluids, bowel rest; ceftriaxone/metronidazole if moderate/severe

mesenteric-ischemia.evidence: Colonic disease checked 2026-10-30: [ACG colon ischemia guideline](https://acgcdn.gi.org/wp-content/uploads/2018/04/ACG-Colon-Ischemia-Guideline-Summary.pdf); acute mesenteric treatment: established emergency framework.

obstructive-sleep-apnea.name: Obstructive Sleep Apnea
obstructive-sleep-apnea.scope: risk factors, clinical features (excessive daytime sleepiness, snoring), polysomnography, CPAP, cardiovascular complications
obstructive-sleep-apnea.core: Recurrent upper-airway obstruction during sleep causes intermittent hypoxemia and arousals, often presenting as loud snoring and excessive daytime sleepiness.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Obesity, large neck circumference, male sex, aging, retrognathia and upper-airway crowding
Alcohol/sedatives worsen collapse; children often have adenotonsillar hypertrophy; risk rises after menopause

rows.label: Clues
items: Witnessed apneas, gasping/choking, unrefreshing sleep, morning headache, nocturia
Resistant hypertension, atrial fibrillation or recurrent drowsy-driving episodes raise suspicion
Children may show hyperactivity, learning problems, enuresis or poor growth rather than sleepiness
Normal awake oxygen saturation does not exclude severe nocturnal disease

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Sleep-related reduction in pharyngeal tone collapses vulnerable airway despite persistent respiratory effort
Intermittent hypoxia and sympathetic surges drive hypertension; fragmentation impairs attention and vigilance

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ **Polysomnography** confirms; screening tools such as STOP-BANG estimate risk, not diagnosis
Uncomplicated high-risk adults → home sleep apnea test acceptable; negative/inconclusive → in-laboratory study
★ AHI **≥5/hour with symptoms/comorbidity**, or ≥15 regardless of symptoms, establishes adult OSA
AHI 5–14 mild, 15–29 moderate, ≥30 severe; pediatric thresholds differ
Cardiorespiratory disease, suspected hypoventilation, chronic opioids or neuromuscular weakness → laboratory polysomnography

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ **CPAP** for symptomatic OSA and most moderate/severe disease; optimize mask fit/adherence
Weight loss, exercise, lateral sleep positioning; avoid bedtime alcohol and sedatives
★ CPAP-intolerant or selected mild/moderate disease → **mandibular advancement device**
Children with adenotonsillar hypertrophy → adenotonsillectomy; selected adults → airway surgery or hypoglossal stimulation
Counsel sleepy patients to avoid driving until controlled; do not rely on stimulants before treating obstruction

rows.label: Complications
items: Systemic hypertension, arrhythmias, stroke risk, pulmonary hypertension in selected patients
Motor vehicle/work accidents, impaired cognition, mood disturbance and perioperative airway risk

rows.label: Prevention
items: Maintain healthy weight, reassess after major weight change; continue PAP around surgery with monitoring

rows.label: Mimics
items: Central apnea: absent respiratory effort during pauses
Narcolepsy: cataplexy and sleep-onset REM features
OHS: persistent daytime hypercapnia

ovarian-torsion.name: Ovarian torsion
ovarian-torsion.scope: Ovarian cyst, ovarian torsion, Doppler ultrasonography, detorsion, cystectomy
ovarian-torsion.core: Abrupt unilateral pelvic pain with nausea and vomiting suggests twisting of the adnexal vascular pedicle, requiring rapid ovarian-preserving surgical assessment.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Ovarian cyst/mass, especially >5 cm; pregnancy, ovulation induction, prior torsion
Functional cysts and mature teratomas common lead points; adolescents may torsion a normal ovary

rows.label: Clues
items: Intermittent severe pain from twisting/untwisting; adnexal tenderness or mass; mild leukocytosis possible
Fever, guarding, peritoneal findings may indicate advanced ischemia; absence does not reassure
Pregnancy test can be positive with torsion; pregnancy does not establish ectopic implantation

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Venous/lymphatic outflow obstruction → congestion and edema, followed by reduced arterial inflow
Dual arterial supply may preserve detectable flow despite clinically important vascular compromise

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ **Pregnancy test** in reproductive-age patients; assess shock, competing surgical diagnoses
★ **Pelvic ultrasound with Doppler** first; transvaginal when feasible, transabdominal in younger adolescents
Enlarged edematous ovary, peripheral follicles, free fluid, twisted pedicle support diagnosis
★ **Normal Doppler flow does not exclude torsion**; no laboratory test reliably rules it out
High clinical suspicion → diagnostic laparoscopy; no serial imaging delay to prove loss of flow

rows.label: Tx
items: NPO, IV access, fluids for dehydration, analgesia/antiemetic; urgent gynecology consultation
★ **Laparoscopic detorsion with ovarian preservation**, even if dark/blue appearance
Cystectomy if safely feasible; friable edematous ovary → defer cyst removal and reassess
Oophorectomy only if unavoidable tissue destruction or compelling malignancy concern; avoid removal for color alone

rows.label: Complications
items: Ovarian infarction, diminished ovarian reserve, infertility, recurrent torsion
Unnecessary extensive resection sacrifices viable ovarian tissue; timely treatment maximizes salvage

rows.label: Prevention
items: ★ Residual cyst → **ultrasound at 6–12 weeks**; persistent significant cyst may need elective cystectomy
Ovulation suppression may reduce recurrent functional cysts; oophoropexy individualized after recurrent torsion

rows.label: Mimics
items: Ectopic pregnancy: extrauterine gestation or concerning pregnancy-location evaluation
Ruptured hemorrhagic cyst: abrupt pain with free fluid; often improves without persistent torsion signs
PID: discharge, cervical motion tenderness, STI risk; bilateral symptoms more typical

palliative-and-hospice-care.name: Palliative and hospice care
palliative-and-hospice-care.scope: Hospice eligibility, pain control, goals of care, surrogate requests
palliative-and-hospice-care.core: Palliative care relieves suffering at any illness stage; hospice centers care on comfort when prognosis and patient goals support a terminal-care benefit.

rows.label: Principle
items: ★ **Patient goals and informed consent** guide intervention burdens; symptom relief remains an obligation
Proportionate opioids for pain/dyspnea ethically permissible despite foreseeable unintended risks

rows.label: Do
items: ★ Ask understanding/values → discuss prognosis → recommend a goal-concordant plan
Assess capacity; use advance directive, then authorized surrogate: substituted judgment/best interests
★ Titrate **opioids** to symptoms; add stimulant laxative for constipation, reassess sedation/respiration

rows.label: Don't
items: DNR ≠ no antibiotics, fluids, nutrition or other desired treatment
Capable patient’s informed wishes override surrogate requests
No nonbeneficial interventions; explain reasoning, offer alternatives, seek ethics review for conflict

rows.label: Exceptions
items: Refractory terminal suffering → proportional palliative sedation, specialist review and consent
Emergency, unknown preferences → stabilize while clarifying wishes; honor documented refusals

rows.label: Traps
items: ★ Hospice: **≤6-month prognosis** if usual course; longer survival permits recertification
Medicare hospice election concerns terminal-illness treatment; unrelated conditions remain treatable
No DNR requirement for hospice; enrollment can be revoked if goals change

palliative-and-hospice-care.evidence: Eligibility checked 2026-10-30: [CMS hospice benefit](https://www.cms.gov/medicare/payment/fee-for-service-providers/hospice); clinical ethics: established teaching.

parasitic-infections.name: Parasitic infections
parasitic-infections.scope: Strongyloidiasis, giardiasis, amebiasis, cryptosporidiosis, ascariasis, schistosomiasis, pinworm (enterobiasis), cysticercosis, eosinophilia workup, antiparasitic therapy
parasitic-infections.core: Exposure, organ pattern, and immune status identify the parasite; eosinophilia favors tissue-invasive helminths rather than intestinal protozoa.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Contaminated food/water, endemic travel, freshwater contact, barefoot soil exposure, household crowding
Steroids/HTLV-1 predispose to Strongyloides hyperinfection; advanced HIV predisposes to persistent cryptosporidiosis

rows.label: Clues
items: Ascariasis: transient cough/eosinophilic infiltrates during larval migration; later intestinal or biliary obstruction
Pinworm: nocturnal perianal itch; household clustering
Cysticercosis: seizures or hydrocephalus; ingestion of **T. solium eggs**, not pork cysts

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Protozoa damage enterocytes; invasive organisms can affect liver, urinary tract, or CNS
Strongyloides autoinfection permits lifelong persistence and dissemination after immunosuppression

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ Unexplained **eosinophilia** → travel/drug history, serial stool O&P, targeted Strongyloides serology
Diarrhea → stool antigen/PCR for protozoa; single routine O&P can miss infection
★ Pinworm → **morning tape test** before washing; stool testing insensitive
Brain MRI/CT for cysticercosis; eye examination before antiparasitics; assess lesion viability and location
Schistosoma: urine/stool eggs; serology useful after endemic exposure when microscopy negative

rows.label: Tx
items: Rehydrate; ascariasis → albendazole; bowel obstruction → surgical evaluation before deworming
Pinworm → albendazole, mebendazole, or pyrantel; repeat after **2 weeks**, treat household simultaneously
★ Viable parenchymal cysticercosis → albendazole ± praziquantel with corticosteroids; seizures → levetiracetam
Calcified brain lesions → no antiparasitic; hydrocephalus → neurosurgical control before cysticidal treatment

rows.label: Complications
items: Strongyloides hyperinfection → gram-negative sepsis, respiratory failure; eosinophilia may disappear
Amebic liver abscess; schistosomiasis → portal hypertension or bladder squamous carcinoma

rows.label: Prevention
items: ★ Screen/treat Strongyloides before **immunosuppression** after endemic exposure
Safe water, sanitation, handwashing, footwear; avoid endemic freshwater and untreated swimming water

rows.label: Mimics
items: IBD: chronic inflammatory diarrhea after infection excluded
Drug hypersensitivity: eosinophilia linked to new medication, rash or organ injury

table.title: Exposure → diagnosis and treatment
rows: Camping; greasy stool, bloating; stool antigen
Soil; larva currens, larvae in stool
Ivermectin; hyperinfection requires prolonged daily treatment
Confirmed E. histolytica without invasive disease

pericardial-disease.name: Pericardial disease
pericardial-disease.scope: Acute pericarditis, pericardial effusion, tamponade, constrictive pericarditis
pericardial-disease.core: Pericardial inflammation, fluid accumulation, or fibrosis produces distinct chest-pain and impaired-filling syndromes; hemodynamic effect depends on accumulation rate.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Viral/idiopathic, autoimmune disease, uremia, malignancy, TB, radiation, cardiac surgery
Early post-MI inflammation or delayed immune-mediated Dressler syndrome; trauma/anticoagulation can cause hemopericardium

rows.label: Clues
items: Pericarditis: sharp pleuritic positional pain, better leaning forward; friction rub may be transient
★ Tamponade: **hypotension, elevated JVP, muffled sounds**, pulsus paradoxus >10 mmHg; triad often incomplete
Constrictive disease: edema/ascites, Kussmaul sign, pericardial knock, prominent y descent

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Inflamed surfaces cause pain; fluid or scar limits diastolic filling and stroke volume
Tamponade equalizes diastolic pressures; constriction exaggerates ventricular interdependence with respiration

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ Pericarditis: ≥2 of **typical pain, rub, diffuse ST elevation/PR depression, new effusion**
Troponin elevation suggests myocardial involvement; CRP supports inflammation; echo assesses fluid and ventricular function
★ **Urgent bedside echo** for suspected tamponade: right-sided chamber collapse, plethoric IVC
Constrictive suspicion → echo, CT/MRI for thickening/calcification; catheterization if diagnosis remains uncertain

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ Tamponade → **urgent pericardiocentesis**; IV fluids bridge; avoid diuresis/positive-pressure ventilation
Purulent/traumatic effusion or recurrent difficult drainage → surgical drainage/window; antibiotics for bacterial cause
Stable effusion → treat cause, serial echo; low voltage alone never determines drainage
High-risk features → admit: fever, large effusion, immunosuppression, anticoagulation, subacute onset, NSAID failure

rows.label: Complications
items: Recurrent inflammation, arrhythmia/myocarditis, obstructive shock; procedural drainage → cardiac injury
Rapid decompression can rarely cause ventricular dysfunction; NSAIDs → GI/renal injury, colchicine → diarrhea

rows.label: Prevention
items: Colchicine course: first episode 3 months; recurrence ≥6 months; taper anti-inflammatory drugs after remission
Exercise restriction until clinical/inflammatory resolution; optimize dialysis for uremic disease

rows.label: Mimics
items: STEMI: regional ST elevation with reciprocal changes; urgent coronary evaluation if uncertain
Restrictive cardiomyopathy: myocardial disease, less respiratory ventricular discordance
PE: thrombotic risk, acute RV strain

table.title: Nonemergency definitive management
rows: Ibuprofen + colchicine; aspirin preferred after MI
Selected low-dose glucocorticoid or IL-1 blockade

peripheral-artery-disease.name: Peripheral artery disease
peripheral-artery-disease.scope: Claudication, aortoiliac (Leriche) disease, critical and acute limb ischemia
peripheral-artery-disease.core: Atherosclerotic limb hypoperfusion ranges from exertional claudication to rest pain, tissue loss, or abrupt limb-threatening arterial occlusion.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Smoking, diabetes, age, CKD, hypertension, dyslipidemia; coronary/cerebrovascular atherosclerosis commonly coexists
AF, aneurysm, graft disease, hypercoagulability predispose acute occlusion

rows.label: Clues
items: Diminished pulses, cool shiny skin, hair loss, dependent rubor, distal nonhealing ulcers
★ **Pain, pallor, pulselessness, paresthesia, paralysis, poikilothermia** → acute limb ischemia
Sensory/motor deficits signal threatened limb; do not await all six findings

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Fixed arterial narrowing limits exercise perfusion; progressive failure reduces resting tissue oxygenation
Acute embolus/thrombus prevents collateral compensation, rapidly injuring nerves and muscle

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ **ABI ≤0.90** confirms PAD; 0.91–0.99 borderline; >1.40 suggests noncompressible arteries
Exertional symptoms with normal resting ABI → exercise ABI; noncompressible vessels → toe-brachial index
Duplex, CTA/MRA define anatomy when revascularization planned; urgent Doppler exam in acute ischemia

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ Symptomatic PAD: **clopidogrel or aspirin + high-intensity statin**, smoking cessation, structured exercise
Cilostazol improves claudication; contraindicated in any heart failure
Refractory disabling claudication → revascularization; chronic limb-threatening ischemia → prompt limb-salvage evaluation
★ Acute ischemia → **IV unfractionated heparin and immediate vascular consultation**; salvageable limb → urgent reperfusion
Low bleeding risk, symptomatic/postrevascularization → low-dose rivaroxaban + aspirin; no full anticoagulation solely for PAD

rows.label: Complications
items: Gangrene, infection, amputation; MI/stroke often dominate long-term mortality
Reperfusion → compartment syndrome, hyperkalemia, rhabdomyolysis; irreversible limb may require primary amputation

rows.label: Prevention
items: ★ **Daily foot inspection**, protective footwear, diabetic foot care, BP/glucose control
Avoid thermal injury to insensate feet; antithrombotic plan after procedures based on bleeding risk

rows.label: Mimics
items: Spinal stenosis: flexion relieves walking pain, pulses preserved
Venous ulcer: medial ankle, edema, pulses intact; neuropathy: sensory loss without ischemic pulse findings

table.title: Clinical stages
rows: Reproducible exercise pain relieved by rest
Buttock claudication, erectile dysfunction, weak femorals

pneumothorax.name: Pneumothorax
pneumothorax.scope: Spontaneous pneumothorax (primary, secondary), tension pneumothorax, needle decompression, chest tube thoracostomy
pneumothorax.core: Pleural air causes acute unilateral pleuritic pain and reduced breath sounds; circulatory compromise indicates tension physiology requiring immediate decompression.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Primary: tall thin young adults, smoking, family history
Secondary: COPD, cystic fibrosis, PJP, interstitial lung disease; trauma/procedures or positive-pressure ventilation

rows.label: Clues
items: Unilateral hyperresonance, dyspnea, asymmetric chest expansion; severity depends on underlying reserve
★ **Hypotension + unilateral absent breath sounds** → tension; tracheal deviation is late
Ventilated patient: sudden desaturation, rising airway pressure, hemodynamic collapse

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Loss of negative pleural pressure permits lung collapse
One-way air entry increases intrathoracic pressure, reducing venous return and causing obstructive shock

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ Unstable tension suspicion → **clinical diagnosis; no imaging delay**
Stable → upright chest radiograph: visceral pleural line with absent peripheral markings
Bedside ultrasound: absent sliding/B-lines supports; lung point highly specific; absent sliding alone nonspecific
CT for uncertain/complex cases; supine radiograph may show deep sulcus rather than apical air

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ Tension → **immediate needle or finger thoracostomy**, then chest tube; oxygen and resuscitation
Needle commonly fourth/fifth intercostal space anterior/midaxillary, or second midclavicular; insert above rib
★ Minimally symptomatic stable primary → **observation**, regardless of size, with reliable follow-up
Symptomatic/large primary → aspiration or small-bore catheter; secondary generally admit, drain if symptomatic/significant
Persistent air leak, recurrence, bilateral disease, or high-risk occupation → VATS bleb treatment/pleurodesis

rows.label: Complications
items: Respiratory failure, tension progression, recurrence; reexpansion pulmonary edema after drainage
Chest tube → bleeding, infection, organ injury; blocked/clamped drain may recreate tension

rows.label: Prevention
items: ★ **Smoking cessation**; avoid flying until radiographic resolution and clearance
Scuba diving contraindicated without specialist assessment/definitive prevention; counsel recurrence warning symptoms

rows.label: Mimics
items: PE: pleuritic pain with preserved lung sliding, embolic risk
Giant bulla: intraparenchymal thin wall; CT if stable uncertainty before tube
Tamponade: shock with pericardial fluid rather than unilateral absent ventilation

pneumothorax.evidence: Conservative care checked 2026-10-30: [BTS pleural guideline 2023](https://doi.org/10.1136/thorax-2022-219784); tension rescue: established emergency teaching.

secondary-hypertension.name: Secondary hypertension
secondary-hypertension.scope: Renal artery stenosis, primary hyperaldosteronism, pheochromocytoma, Cushing syndrome, coarctation of aorta, diagnostic workup
secondary-hypertension.core: Abrupt, unusually young, severe, or resistant hypertension suggests a treatable secondary driver.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Atherosclerosis, fibromuscular dysplasia, renal disease, adrenal tumors, sleep apnea
NSAIDs, oral contraceptives, stimulants, glucocorticoids, licorice; medication nonadherence can mimic resistance

rows.label: Clues
items: ★ **Hypokalemia** suggests mineralocorticoid excess but normal K does not exclude it
Flash pulmonary edema or creatinine rise >30% after ACE inhibitor/ARB → renovascular disease
Endocrine spells, cushingoid appearance, or upper-body hypertension guide cause-specific testing

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Renal hypoperfusion activates RAAS; mineralocorticoid signaling increases distal sodium absorption and potassium loss
Catecholamine/cortisol excess, aortic obstruction, or nocturnal hypoxia increases vascular pressure

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ Confirm **home/ambulatory BP**, adherence, cuff technique; BMP, urinalysis, creatinine, TSH
Sleep-apnea symptoms → polysomnography; abnormal urinary sediment → renal ultrasound and kidney evaluation
★ Biochemical testing precedes adrenal imaging; correct hypokalemia and account for interfering medications
Endocrine Society 2025: suggest **aldosterone screening for all hypertension**, conditional on resources

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ Primary aldosteronism: unilateral → **adrenalectomy**; bilateral → spironolactone/eplerenone
Renovascular atherosclerosis → medical risk reduction; revascularize selected recurrent pulmonary edema or refractory disease
Fibromuscular dysplasia → angioplasty; critical bilateral renal stenosis → avoid ACE inhibitor/ARB
★ Pheochromocytoma: **alpha blockade before beta blockade**, volume expansion, then surgery
Treat cortisol source, repair significant coarctation, use CPAP for OSA; stop contributing drugs

rows.label: Complications
items: Stroke, MI, heart failure, CKD, retinopathy
Unopposed alpha stimulation after beta blockade can cause catecholamine crisis

rows.label: Prevention
items: Monitor renal function/K after RAAS blockers or mineralocorticoid antagonists
Genetic evaluation/family screening for suspected hereditary pheochromocytoma or congenital aortic disease

rows.label: Mimics
items: White-coat hypertension: normal out-of-office readings
Essential hypertension: gradual course without specific endocrine/renal clues

table.title: Targeted workup
rows: Selective suppression test; CT/adrenal venous sampling
Plasma free or urine fractionated metanephrines

secondary-hypertension.evidence: Aldosterone screening checked 2026-10-30: [Endocrine Society 2025](https://www.endocrine.org/clinical-practice-guidelines/primary-aldosteronism-2); other causes: established teaching.

skin-and-soft-tissue-infections.name: Skin and soft tissue infections
skin-and-soft-tissue-infections.scope: Cellulitis, erysipelas, folliculitis, furuncles, carbuncles, lymphangitis, necrotizing fasciitis
skin-and-soft-tissue-infections.core: Skin infection management depends on purulence, systemic illness, and signs of deep tissue destruction.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Skin breaks, tinea pedis, edema/lymphedema, diabetes, obesity, injection drug use
Prior MRSA, crowding, recent hospitalization; surgery or penetrating trauma raises deep-infection risk

rows.label: Clues
items: Warmth, tenderness, erythema; rapidly expanding margins or systemic toxicity require urgent reassessment
★ **Pain out of proportion**, bullae, anesthesia, crepitus, shock → necrotizing infection
Perineal involvement → Fournier gangrene; saltwater exposure → Vibrio, freshwater → Aeromonas

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Nonpurulent infection usually streptococcal; purulent lesions usually S aureus
Fascial spread and toxin-mediated injury → thrombosis, necrosis, sepsis

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ Clinical diagnosis; **bedside ultrasound** if occult fluid collection suspected
Culture drained pus for severe, recurrent, or resistant infection; blood cultures for systemic toxicity
Suspected necrotizing disease → immediate surgical evaluation; imaging must not delay exploration
Low laboratory risk score or absent gas does not exclude necrotizing fasciitis

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ Deep infection → **urgent debridement + vancomycin + piperacillin-tazobactam**, add clindamycin for toxin suppression
Confirmed group A streptococcal necrotizing infection → penicillin + clindamycin
Severe cellulitis/systemic illness → IV cefazolin; MRSA risk → vancomycin
★ Abscess: add **antibiotics** for systemic signs, immunocompromise, extensive disease, or failed drainage

rows.label: Complications
items: Bacteremia, osteomyelitis, septic thrombophlebitis; tissue loss and amputation
Toxic shock, multiorgan failure; recurrent cellulitis worsens lymphatic dysfunction

rows.label: Prevention
items: Treat interdigital fungal infection, manage edema, skin hygiene, protect wounds
Recurrent staphylococcal infections → consider nasal mupirocin + chlorhexidine decolonization; avoid shared razors

rows.label: Mimics
items: Stasis dermatitis: chronic, often bilateral, itchy
DVT: deep swelling without superficial spreading infection; contact dermatitis: pruritic exposure-pattern rash

table.title: Superficial patterns
rows: Incision and drainage; TMP-SMX if needed

skin-and-soft-tissue-infections.evidence: Not checked online; established IDSA-based infection management.

skin-cancer.name: Skin cancer
skin-cancer.scope: Actinic keratosis, squamous cell carcinoma, basal cell carcinoma, melanoma, photoprotection and sunscreen
skin-cancer.core: Changing pigmented lesions or persistent keratinizing, pearly, or ulcerated growths require examination and tissue diagnosis rather than empiric reassurance.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: UV exposure, fair skin, sunburns, tanning beds, older age; immunosuppression particularly increases SCC
Melanoma: numerous/atypical nevi, family/personal melanoma history; may arise without a preexisting nevus
Chronic wounds/scars predispose SCC; acral melanoma occurs regardless of skin pigmentation

rows.label: Clues
items: ★ Melanoma: **ABCDE**—asymmetry, border irregularity, color variation, diameter, evolution; ugly-duckling lesion
Diameter >6 mm concerning, but smaller evolving lesions still require biopsy
Amelanotic melanoma may be pink; inspect soles, palms, nail beds; nail pigment extending onto fold concerning
Rapid growth, bleeding, nonhealing ulcer, fixation, neurologic symptoms, nodes → aggressive or advanced disease

rows.label: Pathophys
items: UV-induced DNA damage → keratinocyte malignancy; melanocyte transformation causes melanoma
AK represents dysplastic keratinocytes with potential progression to invasive SCC

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ Suspicious melanoma → **full-thickness excisional biopsy with narrow margins** to measure Breslow depth
Partial biopsy acceptable when complete excision impractical; avoid superficial sampling that prevents staging
Suspected keratinocyte carcinoma → shave, punch, or excisional biopsy deep enough to assess invasion
Breslow thickness/ulceration guide melanoma staging; sentinel-node discussion generally at ≥0.8 mm or ulceration

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ Localized invasive cancers → **surgical excision**; high-risk/recurrent facial BCC/SCC → Mohs
★ Melanoma → **wide local excision after diagnostic biopsy**; margins depend on depth
Advanced melanoma → specialist immunotherapy, selected BRAF-targeted drugs; avoid destructive treatment before diagnosis

rows.label: Complications
items: BCC: extensive local destruction, rare metastasis; SCC: nodal metastasis, especially high-risk sites/immunosuppression
Melanoma: distant metastases, including brain; immunotherapy → colitis, endocrinopathies, pneumonitis

rows.label: Prevention
items: ★ **Broad-spectrum SPF ≥30**, reapply every 2 hours/outdoors after swimming; shade, protective clothing, no tanning
Self-examination, postcancer follow-up; suspicious lesions require evaluation despite uncertain population-screening benefit

rows.label: Mimics
items: Seborrheic keratosis: waxy stuck-on plaque; atypical lesions still biopsy
Dermatofibroma: firm papule with dimple sign
Benign nevus: stable symmetric uniform appearance

table.title: Nonmelanoma patterns
rows: Assess high-risk features and regional nodes
Pearly rolled edge, telangiectasia, central ulcer
Treat despite slow growth; local invasion

skin-cancer.evidence: Checked 2026-10-30: [AAD melanoma guidance](https://www.aad.org/member/clinical-quality/guidelines/melanoma); established keratinocyte-cancer and photoprotection teaching.

solid-organ-transplantation.name: Solid organ transplantation
solid-organ-transplantation.scope: Hyperacute rejection, acute allograft rejection, chronic allograft rejection, immunosuppressive regimens
solid-organ-transplantation.core: Allograft dysfunction requires urgent distinction among rejection, infection, obstruction/vascular failure, and immunosuppressant toxicity; biopsy usually establishes the rejection mechanism.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: HLA mismatch; sensitization after transplant, transfusion or pregnancy → preformed donor-specific antibodies
Missed immunosuppression, underdosing, drug interactions; rejection can occur late after medication withdrawal

rows.label: Clues
items: Kidney: ↑creatinine; liver: ↑bilirubin/enzymes; heart: ventricular dysfunction; lung: ↓spirometry
Fever, graft tenderness or malaise possible; rejection may be asymptomatic before laboratory abnormalities

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Allorecognition targets donor tissue; immunosuppression balances graft protection against infection and malignancy

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ **Graft ultrasound/Doppler** when relevant → exclude obstruction, thrombosis or vascular compromise
Medication adherence/troughs, cultures and organ-specific viral testing; donor-specific antibodies assess humoral injury
★ **Allograft biopsy** distinguishes rejection from drug toxicity/infection; C4d may support antibody-mediated injury

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ Common kidney maintenance: **tacrolimus + mycophenolate ± prednisone**; regimen varies by organ and risk
Induction in selected recipients → basiliximab or antithymocyte globulin
Steroid-resistant cellular rejection → antithymocyte globulin; coordinate all treatment with transplant team
Never reflexively escalate immunosuppression for unexplained fever before evaluating infection

rows.label: Complications
items: Calcineurin inhibitors → nephrotoxicity, hypertension, neurotoxicity; tacrolimus → diabetes
Mycophenolate → cytopenias, diarrhea, teratogenicity; sirolimus → poor wound healing, hyperlipidemia
Glucocorticoids → diabetes/osteoporosis; immunosuppression → opportunistic infection, skin cancer, EBV-related PTLD

rows.label: Prevention
items: ★ **ABO compatibility, HLA assessment, crossmatch** before transplant; lifelong adherence and trough monitoring
TMP-SMX prophylaxis for Pneumocystis; valganciclovir or preemptive monitoring for CMV according to risk
Vaccinate before transplant; avoid live vaccines during immunosuppression; sun protection and skin checks

rows.label: Mimics
items: Calcineurin toxicity: excessive exposure with compatible biopsy, rather than alloimmune infiltrates
BK nephropathy: kidney transplant, viral PCR and viral inclusions on biopsy
Mechanical graft failure: obstruction/thrombosis demonstrated by imaging

subarachnoid-hemorrhage.name: Subarachnoid hemorrhage
subarachnoid-hemorrhage.scope: Ruptured saccular aneurysm, thunderclap headache, noncontrast head CT, lumbar puncture and xanthochromia, nimodipine, complications
subarachnoid-hemorrhage.core: Sudden headache maximal within seconds, often during exertion, with possible meningismus or collapse: presume subarachnoid hemorrhage until excluded.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Smoking, hypertension, family history, prior aneurysm; autosomal dominant polycystic kidney disease
Ruptured saccular aneurysm usually near circle-of-Willis branch points; cocaine increases rupture risk

rows.label: Clues
items: Vomiting, photophobia, neck stiffness, transient loss of consciousness; sentinel headache may precede major hemorrhage
★ **Painful pupil-involving CN III palsy** → posterior communicating artery aneurysm
Declining consciousness, focal deficits or seizures → high-risk presentation; normal examination does not exclude hemorrhage

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Blood enters subarachnoid space → meningeal irritation, ↑ICP, impaired CSF resorption
Blood-breakdown products and vascular injury contribute to delayed cerebral ischemia

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ **Noncontrast head CT immediately**; sensitivity declines with elapsed time
★ Negative CT >6 hours after onset or neurologic deficit → **LP**, assessing xanthochromia and RBCs
High-quality CT within 6 hours, neurologically intact, expert interpretation → may exclude SAH without routine LP
Confirmed blood → **CT angiography**; negative/inconclusive CTA with suspected aneurysm → catheter angiography
Traumatic tap may show falling RBCs; clearing alone cannot reliably exclude SAH

rows.label: Tx
items: Support airway, reverse anticoagulation, analgesia; severe hypertension → IV nicardipine; avoid hypotension/BP swings
★ **Urgent aneurysm coiling or clipping**, preferably within 24 hours, prevents rebleeding
★ **Enteral nimodipine for 21 days**, maintain euvolemia; no prophylactic hypervolemia
Acute symptomatic hydrocephalus → external ventricular drainage
Secured aneurysm + delayed ischemia → induced hypertension; refractory → endovascular vasodilator/angioplasty

rows.label: Complications
items: Early rebleeding, hydrocephalus, seizures; delayed ischemia typically days 3–14
Hyponatremia from SIADH or cerebral salt wasting; stress cardiomyopathy, arrhythmias, pulmonary edema

rows.label: Prevention
items: Smoking cessation and BP control; specialist screening discussion for ≥2 affected first-degree relatives or high-risk ADPKD

rows.label: Mimics
items: Reversible cerebral vasoconstriction: recurrent thunderclap headaches; segmental angiographic narrowing
Meningitis: fever and inflammatory CSF rather than aneurysmal bleeding
Migraine: usually slower onset, recurrent stereotyped episodes; first thunderclap still needs hemorrhage evaluation

testicular-torsion.name: Testicular torsion
testicular-torsion.scope: Testicular torsion, absent cremasteric reflex, bell-clapper deformity, Doppler ultrasound, surgical detorsion and bilateral orchiopexy
testicular-torsion.core: Sudden unilateral scrotal pain with vomiting in an adolescent is spermatic cord torsion until excluded; salvage depends on immediate action.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Bell-clapper deformity permits excessive intravaginal rotation; often bilateral anatomic predisposition
Pubertal peak; may follow sleep, activity, or minor trauma; neonates can have extravaginal torsion

rows.label: Clues
items: ★ **High-riding horizontal testis, absent cremasteric reflex**, diffuse tenderness and swelling
Pain may present as lower abdominal discomfort without volunteered scrotal symptoms
Prior self-resolving attacks suggest intermittent torsion; symptom resolution does not eliminate recurrence risk
Delayed fever/erythema can occur; no single examination finding reliably excludes torsion

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Cord rotation obstructs venous drainage then arterial inflow → progressive ischemia
Viability falls rapidly with delay; greatest salvage when detorsion occurs within about 6 hours

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ High clinical suspicion → **immediate urologic exploration**, no imaging delay
Equivocal presentation → **color Doppler ultrasound**, comparing perfusion with opposite testis
Reduced/absent flow or twisted cord supports diagnosis; preserved flow possible in partial/intermittent torsion
Urinalysis for infection if uncertain; pyuria does not automatically exclude simultaneous torsion
Examine both testes in boys with unexplained acute abdominal pain; ultrasound cannot overrule compelling clinical findings

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ **Urgent surgical detorsion + bilateral orchiopexy**; orchiectomy only if nonviable
NPO, IV analgesia, fluids as needed; call urology while preparing operation
★ If surgical delay unavoidable → **manual outward detorsion** as bridge; direction sometimes reversed
Pain relief after manual detorsion still requires operative confirmation and fixation; residual twisting possible

rows.label: Complications
items: Infarction, testicular loss, later atrophy, reduced fertility; endocrine function often maintained by opposite testis
Reperfusion does not guarantee long-term viability; follow-up for atrophy

rows.label: Prevention
items: Contralateral fixation addresses shared anatomy; evaluate recurrent episodic scrotal pain promptly
Teach adolescents to report sudden pain immediately despite embarrassment

rows.label: Mimics
items: Epididymitis: gradual pain, urinary/STI symptoms, increased epididymal Doppler flow
Appendix testis torsion: focal superior-pole tenderness, blue-dot sign, preserved testicular flow
Incarcerated hernia: irreducible inguinoscrotal mass, possible bowel obstruction

testicular-torsion.evidence: Not checked online; established urologic emergency assessment and salvage principles.

thrombocytopenia.name: Thrombocytopenia
thrombocytopenia.scope: Evaluation of isolated thrombocytopenia, peripheral smear, immune thrombocytopenia, drug-induced, procedural platelet thresholds
thrombocytopenia.core: Low platelet count requires confirmation and distinction among impaired production, immune destruction, consumption, sequestration, and laboratory artifact.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Recent infection, autoimmune disease, HIV/HCV, lymphoproliferative disease → secondary immune thrombocytopenia
Heparin, quinine, TMP-SMX, vancomycin; alcohol, marrow-suppressive drugs; cirrhosis with splenic sequestration

rows.label: Clues
items: Petechiae, purpura, epistaxis, gingival bleeding; mucosal hemorrhage signals clinically important platelet disorder
★ **Neurologic/renal abnormalities + hemolysis** → thrombotic microangiopathy; systemic illness/coagulopathy → DIC
Heparin exposure + >50% platelet decline, thrombosis, typical 5–10-day onset → HIT

rows.label: Pathophys
items: ITP: IgG-mediated platelet clearance and impaired megakaryocyte production
Drug-dependent immune destruction often causes abrupt severe counts; HIT activates platelets, producing thrombosis

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ **Repeat CBC + peripheral smear**; platelet clumps → citrate tube for pseudothrombocytopenia
Isolated low platelets, normal coagulation, large platelets → ITP after excluding secondary causes
Schistocytes → LDH, haptoglobin, creatinine, coagulation studies; suspected TTP → urgent ADAMTS13 sample
HIV/HCV testing for new ITP; marrow biopsy only atypical cytopenias or suspected marrow disease
4Ts estimates HIT probability; intermediate/high → PF4 immunoassay, functional confirmation

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ Adult ITP **<30,000/µL or bleeding → glucocorticoid**; children without significant bleeding → observation
★ ITP critical bleeding → **IVIG + high-dose steroid + platelet transfusion**
Drug immune thrombocytopenia → stop culprit; persistent ITP → rituximab, thrombopoietin agonist, or selected splenectomy
Suspected TTP → plasma exchange; HIT → stop heparin, start argatroban/nonheparin anticoagulant
Older board LP target: 50,000/µL; current trigger below; neurosurgical targets often ≥100,000/µL

rows.label: Complications
items: Intracranial hemorrhage with severe disease; thrombosis in HIT/TTP
Steroid toxicity, immunosuppression; splenectomy → encapsulated bacterial sepsis

rows.label: Prevention
items: Avoid culprit rechallenge, aspirin/NSAIDs when bleeding risk high; vaccinate before splenectomy

rows.label: Mimics
items: Von Willebrand disease: often normal platelet count with mucocutaneous bleeding
Marrow failure: additional cytopenias, abnormal precursor morphology

thrombocytopenia.evidence: Checked 2026-10-30: [AABB/ICTMG platelet recommendations (2025)](https://www.aabb.org/news-resources/news/article/2025/05/29/aabb-develops-new-platelet-transfusion-guidelines); other hematology principles not separately checked.

transfusion-reactions.name: Transfusion reactions
transfusion-reactions.scope: Acute hemolytic, febrile nonhemolytic, TRALI, TACO, anaphylactic, delayed hemolytic, massive transfusion complications
transfusion-reactions.core: New symptoms during transfusion require stopping the transfusion immediately and evaluating hemolysis, infection and cardiopulmonary compromise.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Prior transfusion/pregnancy → alloantibodies; IgA deficiency with anti-IgA → anaphylaxis
Heart/kidney failure, rapid infusion, older age → circulatory overload

rows.label: Clues
items: Delayed hemolysis: hemoglobin falls with jaundice days–weeks after apparently compatible transfusion
Bacterial contamination: high fever, rigors, profound hypotension; platelets particularly vulnerable
Isolated urticaria without systemic symptoms suggests mild allergic reaction

rows.label: Pathophys
items: ABO mismatch → complement-mediated intravascular lysis; anamnestic antibodies → delayed extravascular hemolysis
TRALI: inflammatory pulmonary capillary leak; TACO: hydrostatic pressure from excess circulating volume

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ Keep IV access with saline; **recheck patient/unit identity**, notify blood bank
Hemolysis workup: DAT, LDH, bilirubin, haptoglobin, plasma/urine hemoglobin; send unit and blood samples
Fever/shock → patient and product cultures; dyspnea → chest radiograph, oxygenation, volume assessment
Suspected febrile nonhemolytic reaction remains diagnosis of exclusion after hemolysis/sepsis evaluation

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ Acute hemolysis → IV saline, support renal perfusion, treat shock/DIC; **never restart unit**
★ Anaphylaxis → **IM epinephrine**, airway support; future washed or IgA-deficient products
TRALI → supportive oxygen/ventilation; diuretics generally unhelpful unless concomitant overload
TACO → upright positioning, oxygen, **IV furosemide**; slow future transfusions
Suspected contamination → broad IV antibiotics; mild isolated allergy → diphenhydramine after clinical reassessment

rows.label: Complications
items: Acute hemolysis → AKI, DIC; severe pulmonary reactions → respiratory failure
Massive transfusion → citrate hypocalcemia, hyperkalemia, hypothermia, dilutional thrombocytopenia/coagulopathy

rows.label: Prevention
items: ★ Bedside identification and crossmatch; leukoreduction reduces febrile reactions
Massive hemorrhage → balanced blood components, temperature and ionized calcium monitoring

rows.label: Mimics
items: Underlying sepsis: symptoms may precede infusion; cultures clarify
Aspiration: event-linked infiltrate without transfusion-specific mechanism

transfusion-reactions.evidence: Not checked online; established transfusion-medicine definitions.

urinary-retention.name: Urinary retention
urinary-retention.scope: Acute vs chronic urinary retention, postoperative etiology, neurogenic bladder, medication-induced, postrenal acute kidney injury, post-void residual volume, bladder catheterization decompression
urinary-retention.core: Inability to empty the bladder requires prompt decompression, identification of obstruction or impaired detrusor function, and monitoring after relief.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: BPH, urethral stricture, prolapse, constipation/fecal impaction, pelvic mass
Recent surgery/anesthesia, opioids, anticholinergics, sympathomimetics; childbirth, diabetes neuropathy, spinal disease

rows.label: Clues
items: Acute: painful suprapubic fullness, inability to void, palpable bladder; postoperative discomfort may be muted
Chronic: hesitancy, weak stream, incomplete emptying, recurrent infection, overflow dribbling
★ **Back pain, saddle anesthesia, leg weakness** → cauda equina emergency; painless retention can be neurogenic

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Outlet resistance or deficient detrusor contraction leaves residual urine, raising intravesical pressure
Persistent high pressure transmits to ureters/kidneys → hydronephrosis and postrenal AKI

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ **Bladder scan/postvoid residual** immediately; catheter measurement if scan unavailable or unreliable
PVR >200 mL suggests incomplete emptying; >300–400 supports retention, but acute diagnosis remains clinical
Urinalysis, creatinine/electrolytes; renal ultrasound for renal dysfunction or suspected chronic high-pressure obstruction
Focused medication, neurologic, rectal/pelvic examination; urgent spinal MRI for compressive neurologic signs
Blood at urethral meatus after pelvic trauma → retrograde urethrogram before blind catheterization

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ **Urethral catheter decompression** promptly; difficult passage → experienced placement, sometimes suprapubic catheter
★ Drain completely; **routine intermittent clamping unnecessary**; monitor hematuria, BP, urine output
BPH → tamsulosin before trial without catheter; stop offending drugs, treat constipation or infection
Neurogenic/chronic incomplete emptying → clean intermittent catheterization when feasible; address obstruction definitively
Postobstructive diuresis >200 mL/hour for 2 hours or >3 L/day → fluids/electrolyte monitoring and replacement

rows.label: Complications
items: UTI, bladder damage, hydronephrosis, kidney injury; catheter → infection/urethral trauma
After decompression: hypovolemia, electrolyte loss, transient bleeding

rows.label: Prevention
items: Review anticholinergic/opioid burden, mobilize postoperatively; voiding trials and early catheter removal when safe

rows.label: Mimics
items: Prerenal/intrinsic oliguria: low bladder volume rather than distended reservoir
Urge incontinence: urgency/leakage with low residual, unlike overflow retention

urinary-retention.evidence: Decompression/diuresis checked 2026-10-30: [AUA urologic emergencies](https://www.auanet.org/Documents/education/medical%20student%20curriculum/Urologic-%20Emergencies-AUA-Med-Student.pdf); remaining content established teaching.

venous-thromboembolism.name: Venous thromboembolism
venous-thromboembolism.core: Unilateral swollen leg or sudden unexplained dyspnea with pleuritic pain; pulmonary embolism severity determined by hemodynamics, not clot size.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Immobilization, surgery, malignancy, estrogen, pregnancy/postpartum, previous VTE, inherited thrombophilia

rows.label: Clues
items: DVT: asymmetric calf tenderness, warmth; PE: tachycardia, hypoxemia, hemoptysis, sometimes normal oxygen saturation
Syncope, elevated JVP, cool extremities → impending RV failure; normal chest radiograph does not exclude PE

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Stasis/endothelial injury/hypercoagulability → venous clot; pulmonary obstruction → V/Q mismatch, RV pressure overload

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ **Wells/pretest probability** first; very low-risk + PERC-negative → no testing
★ Low/intermediate probability → **D-dimer**; negative excludes; positive/high probability → **CT pulmonary angiography**
Age >50: D-dimer threshold age × 10 ng/mL FEU; contrast contraindication → V/Q scan
DVT → compression US; negative proximal scan + persistent suspicion → repeat in 1 week

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ Oxygen/support circulation; unstable and unsafe for CT → bedside **echo**; high suspicion/delayed imaging → anticoagulate
★ Most stable VTE → **apixaban/rivaroxaban**; pregnancy → LMWH; severe renal failure → UFH
Lysis contraindicated/fails → catheter thrombectomy/surgical embolectomy; active intracranial bleeding precludes lysis
Acute proximal DVT/PE + absolute anticoagulation contraindication → temporary **IVC filter**, remove when feasible

rows.label: Complications
items: Postthrombotic syndrome; persistent dyspnea → evaluate chronic thromboembolic pulmonary hypertension
Anticoagulation/thrombolysis → bleeding; heparin → HIT

rows.label: Prevention
items: ★ Major transient trigger → **3 months** anticoagulation; unprovoked/persistent risk → extended course if low bleeding risk
Hospital prophylaxis: LMWH; active bleeding → intermittent pneumatic compression; early mobilization

rows.label: Mimics
items: Cellulitis: predominantly skin erythema, portal of entry
Ruptured Baker cyst: posterior knee symptoms, cyst on US
Pneumonia: focal infiltrate and infectious prodrome

rows: Stable; low PESI/sPESI; no RV injury
Normotensive + RV dysfunction and/or troponin elevation
